messages:
Incident Bot: paging: elevated 5xx rate from private-vpc customers -> gateway timeouts (threshold crossed: 5xx > 3% for 3m). affected route: /v1/generate (redwood-hosted edge -> private-vpc transit). incident_id=INC-2165. Please ack and start triage.
Aisha (oncall): acked. I'm on it. Adding channel and starting triage. Paging infrared.
Aisha (oncall): quick customer impact check: Jordan, can you pull the customer list for private-vpc routes hitting 5xx?
Jordan (prod-support): looking now — approx 7 customers showing increased errors, highest is a mid-market customer in eu-west with heavy burst traffic. Customer-facing SLA risk ~degraded. Notified CS for customers with active sessions.
Nadia (customer-success): thanks Jordan — I'll ping the account owners and tell them we're investigating. ETA for initial update 10m.
Riley (infra-net): I see a spike in SNAT port usage on the private transit NAT appliance. conntrack shows many TIME_WAIT sockets. metrics: ephemeral_ports_used ~ 98%, tcp_retransmits up, NAT gateway CPU normal. Could be ephemeral exhaustion.
Marco (eng-runtime): any recent config changes in runtime that increase connection churn? We rolled a small change 30m ago but it was rate-limiter tweaks only. Rolling back would be noisy.
Aisha (oncall): Riley, can you paste the NAT metrics and conntrack sample?
Riley (infra-net): sure. snippet:
```
NAT ephemeral_used: 98.2%
conntrack_entries: 213k (limit 262k)
TIME_WAIT: 57%
TCP_RETRANS: 12% increase last 10m
flow_count_per_src: lots of short-lived flows from private subnet 10.2.x.x -> 52.x.x (edge)
```
Aisha (oncall): that matches 504s/timeouts. Likely SNAT port depletion causing failures. Any peering flaps?
Riley (infra-net): peering control plane fine. No route flaps. It's an exhaustion pattern, not BGP.
Marco (eng-runtime): do we have per-customer egress pinning (sticky SNAT) enabled on Dedicated? For Private we rely on shared NAT pools. If churn is high, short lived ephemeral ports blow out.
Riley (infra-net): correct. Private uses shared NAT. Dedicated customers get sticky mapping.
Aisha (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) Add short-term extra NAT capacity (spin up another NAT appliance / bigger port pool) 2) Apply temporary egress bypass for the top 3 affected customers to route via dedicated egress path 3) Tune conntrack TIME_WAIT reclaim and reduce idle timers 4) Notify customers and update status. Who can action 1+2?
Riley (infra-net): I can provision an additional NAT instance and expand ephemeral range now. Doing it. Allocating new ephemeral block and updating SNAT rules. ETA ~6m.
Deployer Bot: deploy started: nat-expansion/v1 -> infra-nat-pool (rolling). logs: job 3421 queued.
Riley (infra-net): NAT extra instance provisioned and ephemeral range added: +65k ports. Filling new mapping, watching metrics.
Aisha (oncall): monitor for fall in 5xx after change. Marco, can you add temporary egress route for customer eu-123 and eu-456 to dedicated-egress-2? We want to relieve shared NAT.
Marco (eng-runtime): on it. Creating a canary policy to route requests from those customer API keys to dedicated-egress-2. Pushing policy now.
Deployer Bot: policy push complete: route-policy/customer-eu-123/eu-456 -> dedicated-egress-2 (activated).
Jordan (prod-support): customers eu-123 and eu-456 now show drop in 5xx from 7%->1.2% in last 3m. Others decreased a bit too.
Aisha (oncall): good. Riley, conntrack and ephemeral usage numbers?
Riley (infra-net): ephemeral now 64%. conntrack entries down to 120k. TIME_WAIT down to 22%. 5xx rate cluster-wide dropped from 3.8% -> 0.9% over last 5m.
Aisha (oncall): mitigation successful so far. Next steps: medium-term mitigation (next 24h) — increase NAT autoscaling threshold, add per-customer egress policies for high-QPS customers, and evaluate enabling connection pooling/reuse on runtime side. Marco, can you own runtime changes to reduce connection churn?
Marco (eng-runtime): yes — we'll enable keepalive re-use on edge connectors for private-vpc flows and instrument connection reuse metrics. I'll cut a small rollout to 10% traffic for 2 customers first.
Nadia (customer-success): I'll send a brief customer update: issue caused by NAT ephemeral port exhaustion; we added capacity and temporarily routed the largest customers to dedicated egress; full mitigation ETA 24h. Any text you want me to copy?
Aisha (oncall): include: what happened, steps we took, current status (reduced errors), timeline & recommended action for customers (retry/backoff). Mark as high priority.
Jordan (prod-support): logging note: preserved request_ids for failed samples, attaching examples:
```
request_id: req_01F...
status: 504
src_subnet: 10.2.45.0/24
edge_ip: 52.14.33.44
```
Aisha (oncall): moving to post-incident actions: 1) formal incident ticket INC-2165 with timeline 2) follow-up change to enable per-customer egress for high QPS 3) revisit NAT architecture for private deployments (dedicated pools or per-tenant SNAT) 4) add alert to trigger earlier when ephemeral_port_util > 80% for >2m.
Riley (infra-net): filing infra task to add autoscale NAT and alerting.
Marco (eng-runtime): I'll start a small RFC for connection pooling and re-use with perf numbers.
Aisha (oncall): handoff plan — I'm on call for the next 20m, then Riley will take monitoring and infra follow-ups. Jordan and Nadia will continue customer comms. If anything regresses, page SRE rotation.
Riley (infra-net): acknowledged. Taking handoff in 20m for infra follow-ups.
Nadia (customer-success): customer update sent to affected owners. They appreciate the quick mitigation. One customer asked for a timeline for permanent fix — I'll coordinate.
Aisha (oncall): closing notes: root cause probable SNAT ephemeral exhaustion due to sudden connection churn; mitigated by expanding NAT ports + targeted rerouting; next actions assigned. Will file final postmortem and link here. cc: @exec-ops
Incident Bot: incident INC-2165 status: mitigated -> monitoring. incident_sev: sev2. closed_pager: none.
